rationale: Body-part term filling second slot in the dragon-of-enthumesis five-cave schema (after tongue, before heart). Likely Lyc. for a throat/gullet term, possibly cognate with ⲟⲩⲁϩⲉ 'passage, dwelling-place' used metaphorically for the throat. Distinct from ⲡⲟⲩⲁϥ 'fleshy organ' in glossary.

Body-part term in fourth slot of the dragon's five caves (after heart, before the bond). Possibly related to ⲛⲓϥⲉ 'breathe' or a Lyc. lexeme for lung/respiration apparatus. The order tongue → throat → heart → breath → bond fits a respiratory-circulatory body-mapping.

Lycopolitan reflex of Greek δράκων 'dragon' (with vowel-shift δρα→ⲡⲁⲣⲁ and palatalization). Used here as cosmic-psychological figure identified directly with ⲧⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'the enthumesis of the body' — the dragon IS the body's enthumesis. Standard Manichaean correspondential identification.

proposed_english: I am intent for / I am watchful for
rationale: 1sg disciple-form of attention/eager-watchfulness toward those who shall slay the dragon. Likely Lyc. ⲛⲉⲓ-ⲉⲧⲱⲣϩ̄ on ⲱⲣϩ̄ 'watch, gaze' (cf. ⲣⲉϩⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'watcher' in glossary). Alternative: ⲛⲉⲓⲱⲡ 'I reckon (blessed)' from ⲱⲡ. Confidence low.

Verbal phrase in chapter heading. ⲙⲟⲩⲍ possibly Lyc. for ⲙⲟⲟⲩⲗ/ⲙⲟⲩⲗⲍ̄ 'sink, bow' or a vertical-motion verb. With ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'downward' preserves spatial-directional semantics. Could alternatively be ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' giving 'fill downward' = gluttony.

Verb of casting/scattering paired antithetically with ⲥⲁⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'gather inward.' Likely Lyc. for ⲡⲱⲣⲱ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ or ⲃⲱⲣⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. Captures the dragon's reciprocal action of drawing in and casting forth upon the caves.

In phrase ⲡⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉϩⲃⲓⲛⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'the days of his going-forth.' Possibly Lyc. nominalization on ⲃⲓ/ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' or ⲉⲓ 'come' with ⲛ-epenthesis. Designates departure/exit (likely euphemism for death-passage).
